chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam al-Tanukhi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Adorn yourselves with the carnelian (aqiq), for it is blessed, and whoever adorns himself with the carnelian, it is likely that goodness will be decreed for him.'

key_terms.يُقْضَى لَهُ: It will be decreed/fulfilled for him

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of wearing a carnelian ring in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights the carnelian (aqiq) as a preferred stone for rings, linking its physical presence to spiritual blessing (barakah) and divine favor. The promise of 'al-husna' (the best outcome) underscores the belief that adhering to the Prophet's customs (sunnah) in daily adornments can serve as a conduit for receiving ultimate success in this life and the hereafter.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fazeyl, from Abdul Rahman Bin Zayd Bin Aslam Al Tanouky, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was wearing rings with the carnelian for it is Blessed, and the one who wears a ring with the carnelian, (his needs) would be very quickly fulfilled for him with the goodness’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam al-Tanukiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Wear a ring of carnelian; it is blessed and one who uses a ring of carnelian has a good chance to end up in goodness.’”
